title: Ohio's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The general election for Ohio's 1st Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Democratic Rep. Greg Landsman, first elected in 2022, is seeking a third term against Republican nominee Eric Conroy, a former CIA officer and Air Force veteran endorsed by President Donald Trump. The district, based in the Cincinnati area, was redrawn in October 2025 under a bipartisan redistricting compromise that added Republican-leaning Clinton County while retaining Warren County, making the seat more competitive. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Lean Democratic,' and control of this swing district could factor into the overall battle for the House majority.

polling.pollster: Impact Research (internal poll for Landsman campaign)

polling_note: Only one publicly available poll was identified: an internal poll conducted for the Landsman campaign by Impact Research in November 2025. No independent or neutral polls were found. The poll shows Landsman leading Conroy 49%-43% districtwide.

candidates.name: Greg Landsman
candidates.summary: Greg Landsman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A former public school teacher and Cincinnati City Council member, he led a ballot measure to fund two years of universal preschool in Cincinnati and has focused on reforming congressional ethics, including selling his stocks and suspending his pay during government shutdowns. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and co-chairs the bipartisan What Works Caucus.

candidates.name: Eric Conroy
candidates.summary: Eric Conroy is the Republican nominee for Ohio's 1st Congressional District. A Cincinnati native and Elder High School graduate, he served as an Air Force intelligence officer and later as a CIA case officer with deployments to Afghanistan, Iraq, and Europe. He holds a Master of Public Administration from Columbia University and was endorsed by President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance in the Republican primary, which he won with 71.9% of the vote.

candidates.name: John Hancock
candidates.summary: John Hancock is the Libertarian Party nominee for Ohio's 1st Congressional District. A Cincinnati native, he won the Libertarian primary in May 2026. In February 2026, Hancock was charged with failure to stop after an accident in connection with a December 2025 hit-and-run that critically injured a pedestrian, and he subsequently suspended his campaign. However, he remained on the ballot as the Libertarian nominee after the primary.

forecast.rationale: The incumbent Democrat Greg Landsman has a narrow but meaningful advantage based on available evidence, though uncertainty is substantial. The only public poll — an internal Landsman campaign poll by Impact Research from November 2025 — shows a 49%-43% lead over Republican Eric Conroy, a 6-point margin. Cook Political Report rates the seat as 'Lean Democratic,' and Landsman has incumbency advantage. However, this is a single, campaign-sponsored poll over seven months old. The district was redrawn in October 2025 under a bipartisan compromise that added Republican-leaning Clinton County, making the seat more competitive. Conroy is a credible challenger (former CIA/Air Force) with Trump and Vance endorsements who won the primary with 71.9%. The Libertarian candidate John Hancock suspended his campaign after a legal issue but remains on the ballot, representing a minor factor. With only one dated internal poll and a newly competitive district, confidence is low, but the available signals point to a modest Democratic edge consistent with a lean D rating.
